skill.name: writing-skills
skill.description: Guides agents through test-driven creation, editing, and verification of AI skills using pressure scenarios, focused documentation, and deployment checks.
skill.summary: Create and verify AI skills with a test-driven documentation workflow.
skill.author: obra

security_audit.summary: Static analysis flagged many command, filesystem, and reconnaissance patterns, but review found them to be documentation examples or constrained local helper behavior. No prompt injection, data exfiltration, credential access, or malicious execution intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: The diagram helper uses child_process.execSync, which can concern marketplace reviewers.
remediation.suggestion: Document that it runs only fixed Graphviz commands and accepts DOT through stdin.

remediation.issue: Examples reference hidden Claude and Codex skill directories.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that these paths are illustrative user-owned skill locations, not targets for secret collection.

remediation.issue: The skill uses strong compliance language and pressure scenarios.
remediation.suggestion: Keep examples clearly fenced and label them as tests so agents do not treat them as live instructions.

content.value_statement: AI skills can fail when instructions are vague or untested. This skill guides test-driven skill writing with pressure scenarios and verification loops.
actual_capabilities: Maps RED-GREEN-REFACTOR to skill creation and editing.
Provides structure guidance for SKILL.md frontmatter and sections.
Shows how to write pressure scenarios for agent compliance testing.
Includes examples for Claude skill discovery documentation.
Provides Graphviz conventions and a local diagram rendering helper.
Includes official Anthropic skill authoring guidance as reference material.
limitations: It does not install or publish skills automatically.
The diagram rendering helper requires Graphviz to be installed.
Some guidance assumes Claude or Codex skill directory conventions.
It cannot guarantee model compliance without repeated testing.

use_cases.title: Create A New Skill
use_cases.description: Use the TDD workflow to define triggers, write focused instructions, and verify agent behavior before deployment.

use_cases.title: Repair Weak Skill Guidance
use_cases.description: Use pressure scenarios to find where agents rationalize around rules, then revise the skill to close gaps.

use_cases.title: Review Skill Libraries
use_cases.description: Apply structure, naming, discovery, and testing checks before adding skills to a shared repository.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a new AI skill for this situation. Identify the trigger, intended user behavior, and the first pressure scenario to test.

prompt_templates.title: Write Pressure Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Create three pressure scenarios for this skill. Include time pressure, sunk cost, authority pressure, and clear success criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Skill Discovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this skill description and SKILL.md outline. Make the trigger clearer without summarizing the full workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Audit A Skill Before Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this skill using the RED-GREEN-REFACTOR checklist. Identify missing tests, unclear rules, rationalization gaps, and release blockers.

output_examples.input: A request to create a skill for flaky async tests.
output: A concise skill trigger focused on race conditions and inconsistent test results.
Three pressure scenarios that test whether an agent avoids timing shortcuts.
A release checklist covering baseline testing, verification, and documentation clarity.

output_examples.input: A draft skill that agents keep ignoring under deadline pressure.
output: A list of the rationalizations found during baseline testing.
A revised rule section with explicit counters to those rationalizations.
A re-test plan that confirms the revised skill changes agent behavior.

output_examples.input: A team wants to standardize several skill documents.
output: Recommended naming, description, and file organization changes.
A testing plan for discipline skills and technique skills.
Notes on when to split heavy references into separate files.

best_practices: Run a baseline scenario before writing or editing a skill.
Keep the description focused on triggers, not the workflow.
Retest after every change that closes a rationalization gap.
anti_patterns: Writing skill instructions before observing a real failure.
Adding long process summaries to the skill description.
Using generic examples that do not create realistic pressure.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps authors create AI skills that agents can discover, read, and follow under pressure.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Claude Code directory examples and guidance for Claude skill discovery.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The core workflow applies to Codex skills, although some examples use Claude directory names.

faq.question: Does it create the skill files for me?
faq.answer: No. It guides planning, writing, testing, and review. File creation still happens through your normal tools.

faq.question: Why does it require baseline testing?
faq.answer: Baseline testing shows how agents fail without the skill, so the document can address real behavior.

faq.question: When should I use the diagram helper?
faq.answer: Use it when a skill contains Graphviz flowcharts that a human reviewer needs to inspect visually.
